core_obligations: Note that the first two conditions are equivalent because the spaces are affine (proof lines 6707-6709).
Show that in either case the morphism is representable by algebraic spaces, hence affine, and that the source is therefore countably indexed as well (proof lines 6709-6713).
Write both spaces as formal spectra of weakly admissible algebras, express the morphism as a continuous ring map, and conclude the equivalence from the comparison lemma (proof lines 6713-6724).
proof_roadmap: The first two conditions agree (proof lines 6707-6709).
Countable indexedness of the source (proof lines 6709-6713).
Formal spectra, the ring map, and the comparison (proof lines 6713-6724).
difficulty_reason: For a morphism of affine formal algebraic spaces with countably indexed target, the lemma asserts the equivalence of being locally of finite type, being of finite type, and corresponding to a morphism of complete weakly admissible rings satisfying the finite typeness conditions of an earlier lemma (statement lines 6694-6705). The proof first notes that the first two conditions agree because both spaces are affine, and then derives a consequence that the statement needs: in either case the morphism is representable by algebraic spaces by definition, hence affine by the earlier structure result, so the source is countably indexed as well by the statement on affine morphisms over an affine formal algebraic space (proof lines 6707-6713). With both spaces countably indexed they are formal spectra of weakly admissible algebras, the morphism corresponds to a continuous map of those algebras, and the equivalence follows from the lemma comparing finite typeness of the morphism with tautness and topological finite typeness of the ring map (proof lines 6713-6724). The claim is H2: the transfer showing that the source inherits countable indexedness is a real step of the argument -- it is what makes the cited comparison applicable -- and the remaining reduction is explicit.
